NO DAMAGE IS REPORTED AT THIS TIME. PILOT DIVERTING TO BDL PER CMPANY REQUEST. TWO PHOTOS. Smithsonian Wildlife Identification Comments: Sample received from both reports filed for this strike, one from bird on the runway and one from the aircraft found feathers. Both samples = Herring Gull FROM MOR: VXP323 DEPARTED KHVN. REPORTED A BIRD STRIKE THAT HIT THEIR NOSE THAT SET OFF LLWS ALARM TO Y90. Y90 DECLARED EMERGENCY AND RELAYED INFORMATION TO BDL TOWER. CRASH PHONE RANG AT 1415Z. EMERGENCY PERSONEL TOOK POSITION. VXP323 HELD IN THE AIR TO BURN FUEL THEN LANDED RWY 6 AT 1455Z, TAXIIED TO GATE 24 UNDER THEIR OWN POWER. LC RELAYED PHONE NUMBER FOR VXP323 TO CALL Y90 AS REQUESTED FOR DAMAGE REPORT AND FURTHER INFO. JSEN NOTIFIED. VXP323 (Avelo) IFR B737 departure from HVN to FLL encountered a bird strike on departure, requested to divert to BDL, and was handed off from N90.  N90 reported that the pilot took evasive maneuvers and the pilot believes there may be damage to the aircraft.  Pilot also stated the strike resulted in a wind shear alarm in the cockpit.  An emergency was declared by Y90 with 144 souls on board and 19,700 lbs of fuel-- BDL ATCT, DEN, JSEN advised.  Aircraft entered holding to burn fuel for appropriate landing weight, then landed RY6 at 1455Z without incident.  UPDATE 1522Z: Pilot called landline and advised no visible damage to the nose.  Bird struck the PITOT tube off captains side and bird remains are inside the PITOT tube, which coincides with the wind shear alert they received on departure.  Aircraft will be receiving maintenance at BDL.  Pilot clarified there was no evasive maneuver due to the low altitude of the strike, (approximately 750 feet).  Pilot stated the strike occurred north of the departure runway, possible off airport property.  HVN reported to N90 no remains found.
